title: Wrestling, not dancing
hookLine: the art of living is more like wrestling than dancing (Meditations 7.61)

cards: Watch a ballet dancer. Every step is planned. The music tells her what comes next, the floor is smooth, and nobody runs onto the stage to knock her down.
Now watch a wrestler. He has a plan too, but it lasts a moment. Then a hand grabs his ankle from a direction he didn't expect, and everything depends on whether he can keep his feet.
It's tempting to hope life will be a dance. Marcus Aurelius had other news.

teach.b: Meditations seven, sixty-one, in George Long's translation: "The art of life is more like the wrestler's art than the dancer's." Why?
Because life calls for standing ready and firm against blows that come suddenly and without warning. Dancing is beautiful; Marcus isn't mocking it.
But a dance is choreography. If life were a dance, you could rehearse your way to perfection, and any surprise would be a failure.
It's easy to live that way: plan the perfect week, and call it ruined when the car breaks down on Tuesday. A wrestler expects to be grabbed. Surprise isn't failure; it's the sport.
The skill isn't avoiding contact but balance under contact: low center of gravity, knees bent, weight ready to shift. A wrestler who gets thrown gets up, and the getting up is part of the art.
On this path, book seven is the wrestler's book, and this line is why. You don't become steady by hoping nothing hits you. You become steady by practicing what to do when it does.
That's what these short lines from Marcus are for. Back quickly. Emerald.
Holds and stances, drilled in quiet so they're ready in the scramble.
When the sudden grab comes, a bad phone call or an unfair word, you won't have time to think. You'll only have what you've practiced.

how: Readers of Marcus often use the wrestler image to expect surprises rather than resent them, rehearsing short principles in calm moments so they are ready when something sudden happens.

o: Marcus's picture of life: staying steady under sudden grabs
life as a steady dance, each step planned ahead
Marcus's call to beat every rival you meet in life

s: he only says life is more like wrestling, because blows come suddenly.
7.61 says life needs standing ready for sudden, unexpected blows
that's why it's more like the wrestler's art.
for a wrestler, being surprised means failure
surprise is the sport; the skill is staying balanced through it.

games.q: you planned the perfect week, and on Tuesday the car breaks down. what does the wrestler do?
o: stay steady, adjust, and keep going.
games.why: Meditations 7.61: the art of life is more like wrestling than dancing; it means standing ready and firm against sudden blows.

practice: Feel your weight settle into the seat and the floor, and breathe into your center, low in your belly. Bring to mind one struggle you're in right now and picture it grabbing at you.
Instead of bracing stiff, bend your knees in your mind, lower your center, and stay on your feet: not winning, just steady.

wordCard.voice: Wrestling. Marcus's picture of the art of life: not a planned dance, but a sport of staying steady against sudden grabs. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: the wrestler's art, which Marcus compares to the art of living in 7.61.

carryVoice: Your line: a hand grabs his ankle. Knees bent, ready for the next one. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: The art of life is more like the wrestler's art than the dancer's
